answer: A routing seat should cost a one-shot heat coupon, not a minted alias. I lock 51.3 POA on kiln run KR-28 for 38 minutes and must forge a 0.88 kg copper coupon. A 6 mm probe has to wander a 9-leg zigzag from the thick vertex to the sprue, while two unaffiliated clocks hash the pyrometer series (780-805 C, 0.4 C rms vs the shop curve) plus a 1.9-2.3 g mass loss. A zigzag matching another run within 3 mm, or a mass-loss miss, slashes 70 percent and retires KR-28. A cracked thermocouple mid-run freezes the remainder 15 hours and forces a new alloy, never a replay of the same heat.
